answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps interaction graphs into an atlas and conducts topological cut verifications. If a cut creates a sparse bottleneck, decentralized auditors inspect the cluster. Auditing triggers game-theoretic multi-agent audits: any fraudulent signal results in irreversible stake slashing. This forces an attacker to deploy exponentially increasing collateral across each identity to simulate a genuine dense meadow of agents.
